info.description: Versioned REST API for DAW UIs and agents (conventions: docs/STUDIO_API_V1_CONVENTIONS.md). Errors use one envelope; mutations take Idempotency-Key; revisions are ETags; lists use cursor pagination. The apply is done only once the live engine plays the new version (engine_status 'swapped'; get_clip_waveform then reports revision); if the engine cannot load it the job fails with engine_swap_failed, engine_status = the engine's code and NOTHING committed (rolled_back=true; the clip keeps its previous audio and revision; retry with the same key). A tempo-stretched clip is 409 in_place_unsupported_source. Selection: start_ms/end_ms (timeline ms) OR start_frame/end_frame (+ sample_rate), not both; a range past the clip is clamped to it. crossfade_ms (0-100) blends original -> processed inside the selection. Regions over 120 s are refused (region_too_long). The clip must be loaded in the live session. Runs as a job: waits up to wait_sec (default 20, max 50); 200 with status 'done' and the result, or 202 with status 'queued'/'running', job_id and a Location to poll. The Idempotency-Key header doubles as the apply's idempotency_key (a committed apply answers replay; after undoing, apply again with a NEW key or get idempotency_key_used). Undo (split): POST undo.inverse_ops to clips:batch. If-Match takes the timeline revision (412 timeline_revision_conflict); a clip that changed mid-apply is 412 conflict. A result peaking ABOVE 0 dBFS (by more than 0.0001 dB) is refused (409 would_clip) unless allow_clipping=true; a peak of exactly 0 dBFS is allowed (it is stored unclipped). dry_run=true plans only. Live-engine failures keep a specific code: 503 engine_session_contended (another project of this account took the account's live engine; retry after Retry-After), engine_session_not_found, engine_restarting; otherwise the engine's own code, with details.engineReason when it gave one. Charged to the Mozart AI burst guard, like MCP.

The response ETag is the new timeline revision. applied_ops is the integer count of applied ops. Live engine: after the commit the backend reads the session's clip list back and checks every op landed (removed ids gone; updated / inserted / restored ids present once, on their lane, at the committed timing); any mismatch is engine_reload_required=true with engine_divergent [{id, reason}] and reload = the engine:reload operation to call. engine_loaded=false means no live session holds the project (nothing to mirror; the next load reads the saved clips). undo.inverse_ops is the batch that undoes this one (same op shape, `expected` = the post-batch state, reverse order): POST it back here to undo. inserted lists every inserted/restored clip {clipId, laneId, sourceId, startMs, durationSec, audioOffsetSec, engine_attached}: a pasted clip with engine_attached=true plays at once, so no attachClipToSession call is needed. A batch that committed is never reported as a 5xx: when a post-commit step fails the 200 carries postCommitError and engine_reload_required=true, and the Idempotency-Key replays that result (replay=true in the body plus the Idempotent-Replayed: true header). Lane changes are NOT supported here (ops keep each clip on its lane): use POST clips/{clip_id}:move-to-lane for cross-lane moves (e.g. a cross-track paste).

Access is re-checked for the uplink's whole life, not only here: on every take_start / take_restart and every few seconds Mozart re-reads the user's write role and the app's grant. A refused take answers {type:'take_refused', take_id, code, status, closing} (codes: oauth_grant_revoked, project_write_forbidden, peer_delegation_write_required = this offer's access window ended, re-offer; permission_lookup_unavailable = retry; take_id_in_use; take_id_invalid) and a revoked or expired uplink is closed ({type:'uplink_revoked', code}). A take_id is single-use: one that already names a take on the engine (saved or not) is refused with take_id_in_use. get.summary: Get the monitoring peer's late ICE candidates

post.description: SDP offer for the project's live audio session (startAudioMonitor first); returns Mozart's SDP answer (the rick webrtc offer). Audio then flows Mozart -> client directly. By default the answer waits until the engine has a relay-capable ICE candidate (about 1-2 s, at most about 4 s), so restrictive networks connect. With trickle=true the engine answers as soon as it has a server-reflexive candidate (a few hundred ms) and response.trickle=true; then poll getMonitorCandidates and addIceCandidate each later candidate (the TURN relay one that cellular / restrictive networks need) until complete=true or the peer connects. response.trickle=false means the engine waited as before (nothing to fetch). See /docs/realtime.html#monitor-latency. The peer runs on the engine as this user: with daw:write and the owner/editor role the answer has peerGrant=write and the peer's data channels accept the Studio's fast input (mozart-control: transport_play/pause/seek, set_track_gain/muted/soloed, set_plugin_param, midi_note, midi_all_notes_off, sample_preview, sample_preview_release, live_hold; mozart-editor, negotiated id 100: editor.pointer/scroll/type), re-checked live against the role and the OAuth grant until peerGrantExpiresAt. Otherwise peerGrant=read (audio, clock, meters, editor frames). peerGrant is what the engine confirmed it applied; when it cannot confirm, the peer is closed and the call answers 502 peer_delegation_unconfirmed. An engine that is still being updated answers 503 engine_update_required before anything is sent to it (your existing peer keeps running; retry shortly). An account that never completed a sign-in the engine can re-check answers 403 peer_identity_unavailable. Once mozart-control is open the engine pushes engine_clock frames on it every 100 ms (getTransportClock fields + rtp_sync). Create the data channels before the offer so it has an m=application section; re-offer with the same client_id to renew (the old peer is replaced); stopAudioMonitor closes it and setAudioMonitorQuality changes its bitrate live. client_id is yours: it is scoped to your user, so it can never address another member's peer. Should the engine still report the id as another peer's, the call answers 409 webrtc_client_id_in_use: nothing was replaced, send the offer again with a new client_id. See /docs/realtime.html#fast-input.

Not idempotent (each call plays). Pre-arm (Session clip launch): arm_only=true with client_id (your monitoring peer) compiles the pattern and resolves its samples WITHOUT playing; the reply carries armedSignature (yours, else a generated one) and the engine's response {ok, armed: true, armed_signature, prepare_ms, session_epoch}. Then start it with ONE message on that peer's mozart-control channel: {type: "pattern_preview_start", project_id, key, seq, armed_signature, preview_request_id, repeat_count?, gain?, phase_offset_sec?, lead_sec?} -> {type: "pattern_preview_ack", ok, key, seq, armed_signature, preview_request_id, engine_time_sec, ...} (code not_armed: re-arm, or call this op without arm_only; stale_preview_request: that id was already stopped). Stop it with {type: "pattern_preview_stop", project_id, key, seq, preview_request_id}. Over REST, armed_signature (with the same client_id) without arm_only starts the armed preview, and compiles pattern instead when the arm is gone. An arm is kept per peer, one at a time (a new arm replaces it), for up to 10 minutes and until the engine session reloads; re-arm after each edit. A peer keeps up to 16 arms at once (one per signature; the oldest is dropped). This single preview replaces everything sounding when it starts (scene layers included); to play several together at one time, arm each and use launchPatternPreviews (see /docs/realtime.html#pattern-launch). Show the take as saving and call again with the same take_id (idempotent). 404 recording_take_not_found. The take's audio is the client's own live-ingest microphone uplink (sendLiveIngestOffer: WebRTC, client -> Mozart directly; pass lane_id there to pick the record lane); no audio ever passes through this API. Sequence: (1) sendLiveIngestOffer with the microphone track and the negotiated data channel (id 200, label mozart-live-ingest); send {type:'keepalive', id} on it every 5 s; (2) startRecording; (3) on the data channel send response.audio.take_start plus your own take_id ([A-Za-z0-9_-], <= 96, no '__', single-use: a reused id is refused with take_refused take_id_in_use): {type:'take_start', take_id, mode:'record', song_start_sec, lane_id?} (lane_id here, a lane of this project or 404, is echoed into it; default = the user's own vocal lane); (4) {type:'take_stop', take_id, song_end_sec} when done (song_end_sec = song_start_sec + the take's length in seconds; it bounds the saved clip); (5) finalizeRecording(take_id, wait_for='placed'): the clip is on the lane in about a second, then it is scanned and promoted as the calling user exactly like a Studio take. Existing clips on the lane are kept: an API take on a normal project only adds its clip. In a live room / Endless session the room's one-take-per-lane rule applies (the take replaces the earlier takes on its lane at take_start). The take is placed on the song timeline from song_start_sec. Like Record in any DAW, a take_start (mode 'record', engine_mode true or false) on a STOPPED transport rolls the transport from song_start_sec (take_started.started_transport=true); send sync song_sec from the engine clock as it moves. A take whose song clock still never moved (every sync at the same song_sec) is saved whole from song_start_sec, never cut to the last seconds. count_in_beats with start_transport=true rolls it on the count-in boundary instead. See /docs/realtime.html#recording-takes. A failed start stops a transport it started (start_transport) and parks the playhead back. Count-in: count_in_beats (1-8) is the Studio's count-in (Mozart /transport/record-arm, wait=true): the metronome clicks that many beats and the reply returns AT the recording boundary with response.count_in {beats, beat_samples, bpm, first_click_sample, recording_start_sample, recording_start_position_seconds, audio_device_sample, sample_rate, transport_started, ...} (also response.count_in_beat_samples / count_in_bpm, the legacy names). Samples are on the engine's audio-device clock: last click -> boundary = one beat. seek_seconds parks a stopped transport there first, start_transport=true rolls it on the boundary, bpm (20-400) is the count-in tempo. 0 or absent = armed at once. While anybody (a browser, a live room, another API client) records on the engine the start is 409 recording_in_progress and that take is untouched. Keepalive: the engine keeps the arm while the uplink's data-channel keepalive is fresh or the caller polls getRecordingStatus, drops it 60 s after the last sign of life and never holds it longer than the 20 minute take limit. finalizeRecording ends the arm (response.engine_disarmed) but never a take a browser or live-room member armed or joined. 409 engine_update_required: the engine host does not support API recording yet.

put.description: A one-segment constant tempo map at bpm (20-400); meter and pattern meters are kept. A map with ramps or several segments is refused with 409 tempo_map_not_constant (edit it with PUT timing-map). If-Match = the timing-map revision you read (412 if it moved). mode=keep_time (default, unchanged behaviour): clips and pattern placements keep their start time. mode=stretch_audio (Logic "Adapt Project Tempo"): every audio clip is time-stretched with pitch preserved through the per-clip tempo render pipeline (always from its original audio), a backing that is not yet a clip is first converted into one full-length clip, and every clip and pattern placement start (and placement length) is scaled by old_bpm/new_bpm around project time 0, so content stays on the same bar and beat. Hidden loop repeats tile their parent's measured rendered length; automation is rescaled (clip envelopes by the clip's measured render ratio, pattern-placement and lane envelopes by old/new); when the backing audio is stretched the bar-ruler anchor (backing.firstBeatSec) follows it; timed custom lyrics (time_ms) scale by old/new. After the save the live engine session is reloaded in the background with retries (engine.reload 'pending' until it finished); if it still cannot be reloaded the job is status succeeded with engine_reload_required=true (call reloadEngineSession). stretch_audio is a job: 202 with job_id, status and a Location to poll (getTempoStretchJob). Renders are staged: the project keeps playing exactly as before until every render succeeded, then ONE transaction swaps the audio, positions and tempo together (it is never half-stretched; a failed render changes nothing). While the job is queued or running, clip, pattern-placement, tempo-map, automation and lyrics writes on the project answer 409 tempo_stretch_in_progress (details.job_id); an edit made anyway (directly on the live engine) fails the job with tempo_stretch_project_changed and is kept. undoTempoStretchJob restores the tempo, positions and original audio exactly. One stretch costs one hourly tempo request (none when it could not start). 409 tempo_stretch_in_progress while another stretch runs (one per project); 422 tempo_out_of_range when an already-stretched clip would leave 20-400 BPM.
